The use of a single oral dose of activated charcoal has become a widespread method of preventing the absorption of in- gested compounds and may be superior to gastric emptying. The American Academy of Clinical Toxicology (AACT) and the Eu- ropean Association of Poisons Centres and Clinical Toxicolo- gists (EAPCCT) consider1 that activated charcoal may be used if a patient presents within 1 hour of ingesting a potentially toxic amount of a poison known to be adsorbed by charcoal. There are insufficient data to support general use beyond 1 hour after in- gestion.1-3 In addition, multiple oral doses of activated charcoal have been found to enhance the elimination of some drugs and toxic substances even after systemic absorption.
